newsitem.title: UK: Proton says it bought control of Lotus.
newsitem.headline: Proton says it bought control of Lotus.

text.p: Malaysia's Proton said Wednesday it has acquired a controlling interest in Lotus Group, the British sports car maker, for 51 million pounds ($82.7 million) in cash.
The deal ends months of uncertainty for the British company, whose owner Italian entrepreneur Romano Artioli has been seeking a major investor for most of this year.

Yahaya Ahmad, chairman of Proton's parent DRB-HICOM and one of Malaysia's most influential businessmen, is taking a 16.25 percent personal stake in Lotus, alongside Proton's 63.75 percent interest, the company said.

"The change in ownership will not affect the way that the company's businesses are managed, including Lotus Engineering, which will continue to pursue its role as a leading independent supplier of design engineering services and technology," Proton said in a statement.
It added that through the acquisition it was keen to "expand its collaborative activities with the manufacturers to enhance the synergy and to develop the exchange of technology."
